1 · Intro

When to use it.

Not every person you bring on needs the same checks. Federal law requires a Form I-9 for every employee, and Vanderbilt requires background checks for some worker types.

Get it wrong and you either delay a start or start someone without required clearance.

Use this whenYou are bringing on a new person and need to know which checks must be complete before or soon after they start.

Watch-outs

  • Section 1 cannot wait for the three-day window; it is due on day one.
  • New York requires non-criminal background checks before any conditional offer.
  • Open item: confirm who completes Section 2 of the I-9 at Vanderbilt, in which system, and how remote hires are handled.

I-9 and background check requirements by worker type

Use when: You are bringing on a new person and need to know which checks must be complete before or soon after they start. · System: Process

  1. Identify the worker type first.
  2. Look up the requirement in the table.
  3. Have the employee complete I-9 Section 1 by the first day of work.
  4. Complete I-9 Section 2 within three business days of the start date.
    • Example: start Monday, Section 2 due Thursday.
  5. Wait for clear to start when a background check applies.
  6. Request checks manually when there is no requisition.
